findings.issue_text: [Critical/security] services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/UsersResource.java:448 — searchForUser treats an empty result from getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() as 'no restriction', but empty is also returned when the admin has no view permission and no granted groups; with the !auth.users().canView() guard and the .filter(usersEvaluator::canView) safety net removed, a query-users-only admin now gets a completely unrestricted search exposing every realm user (usernames, emails, attributes), where the old code returned nothing. The PR's own new test (GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest.testCanViewUserByViewGroupMembers first assertion) encodes the old restricted behavior and will fail against this implementation.
[Critical/security] The same empty-set overload in UsersResource makes the parallel getUsersCount branches report 0 while the list endpoint returns everyone.

[High/security] services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:47 (canManage()) — the global manage check evaluates hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE), so a view-scope grant on the Groups resource type satisfies canManage()/requireManage(); a view-only admin can therefore create top-level groups (POST /groups), a privilege escalation. canManage(GroupModel) correctly uses MANAGE only; this looks copied from canView(), and the javadoc added to GroupPermissionEvaluator.canManage() repeats the same mistake.

[Medium/bug] services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:~160 (hasPermission) — the type-level ('all-groups') fallback is only applied when resourceStore.findByName(...) finds no group-specific resource; once a per-group resource exists, an admin holding an all-groups MANAGE/VIEW grant is silently denied on that group since policies attached to the type-level resource are never consulted. Grants should union, not be shadowed by the existence of an unrelated resource.

[Medium/security] services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:~96 (getGroupIdsWithViewPermission) — the method only scans per-group resources and never consults the type-level resource; an admin granted VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS on 'all groups' (type-level permission, no per-group resources) gets an empty set, which results in an unrestricted user search exposing all users (including those in no group) instead of only group members.

[Medium/data] services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:~180 + AdminPermissions.java:~94 — no cleanup path exists for V2 group authorization data: GroupPermissionsV2 throws UnsupportedOperationException for all permission-management/lifecycle methods, while AdminPermissions.registerListener (registered exactly when V2 is active) still performs cleanup by calling groups().setPermissionsEnabled(group, false) on group removal; deleted groups therefore leave orphaned 'Groups'-type resources and policies behind (which getGroupIdsWithViewPermission keeps scanning), and if the listener resolves to the V2 implementation, every group deletion will throw.

[Medium/performance] services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/GroupResource.java:177 and GroupsResource.java:112 — the cached canViewGlobal short-circuit was removed, so filter(...::canView) now runs a full authorization evaluation (resource lookup + policy evaluation) per group element; for admins whose access comes from a type-level grant, getSubGroupsStream(search, exact, -1, -1) loads all subgroups and each one triggers a separate policy evaluation before pagination. canView() should be computed once and used to short-circuit the filter.

[Medium/security] rest/admin-ui-ext/src/main/java/org/keycloak/admin/ui/rest/BruteForceUsersResource.java:147 — the rewritten searchForUser has the same empty-set overload (empty set → no UserModel.GROUPS attribute → unrestricted search) and, unlike the old UsersResource code, never had a per-user canView filter; the hole is pre-existing, but since these lines are being rewritten to the shared new pattern it should be fixed here too, otherwise admins without view permission get the full user list from the brute-force search.

[Low/test_gap] tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/authz/fgap/GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest.java — there is no negative test asserting that an admin holding only the VIEW scope on the Groups resource (no MANAGE) is denied group creation/update/manage; such a test would have caught the canManage() scope bug.

[Low/doc_defect] services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionEvaluator.java:~147 — the javadoc for getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() says '@return Stream of IDs of groups with view permission', but the method returns Set<String>, not a Stream.

goldens.comment: In GroupPermissionsV2.canManage(), the permission fallback checks for both VIEW and MANAGE scopes (hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)), but canManage() should only grant access for MANAGE scope, not VIEW. This means users with only VIEW permission on groups can pass the canManage() check, granting them write access they should not have. The canView() method correctly checks both VIEW and MANAGE, but canManage() should only check MANAGE.

In getGroupIdsWithViewPermission, hasPermission is called with groupResource.getId() and the same groupResource.getId() is added to granted, but hasPermission resolves resources by name (treating the argument as a group id) and the GroupPermissionEvaluator contract says this method returns group IDs that are later used as UserModel.GROUPS and in getUsersCount group filters. This mismatch means per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions may not yield the expected group IDs for filtering and counts, and evaluation may effectively only look at the type-level 'all-groups' resource; consider revisiting whether this should operate on the underlying group ids (resource names) instead so it aligns with the JPA queries and the interface contract.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Critical/security] services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/UsersResource.java:448 — searchForUser treats an empty result from getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() as 'no restriction', but empty is also returned when the admin has no view permission and no granted groups; with the !auth.users().canView() guard and the .filter(usersEvaluator::canView) safety net removed, a query-users-only admin now gets a completely unrestricted search exposing every realm user (usernames, emails, attributes), where the old code returned nothing. The PR's own new test (GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest.testCanViewUserByViewGroupMembers first assertion) encodes the old restricted behavior and will fail against this implementation.

adjudication.rationale: In UsersResource.searchForUser the diff removes both the `!auth.users().canView()` guard and the `.filter(usersEvaluator::canView)` restriction, and now only sets `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, groupIds)` when `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` is non-empty. When the caller cannot globally view users and has *no* granted group view permissions, `groupIds` is empty, so no restriction attribute is set and the code returns `session.users().searchForUserStream(...)` unfiltered. From the diff alone this creates the exact ambiguity the finding describes: empty set can mean either “no restriction” (global view) or “no permitted groups”, and the previous safety net filter is gone. This is consistent with the new test’s expectation that a query-only admin initially sees no users, which would be violated if the stream is unrestricted.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Critical/security] The same empty-set overload in UsersResource makes the parallel getUsersCount branches report 0 while the list endpoint returns everyone.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows getUsersCount now passes `auth.groups().getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` instead of `getGroupsWithViewPermission()`, but it does not show any “empty-set overload” behavior or that an empty set makes the count return 0. The claim that the count endpoint reports 0 while the list endpoint returns everyone cannot be verified from this diff alone (the underlying `session.users().getUsersCount(...)` overload behavior is not present here).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:~160 (hasPermission) — the type-level ('all-groups') fallback is only applied when resourceStore.findByName(...) finds no group-specific resource; once a per-group resource exists, an admin holding an all-groups MANAGE/VIEW grant is silently denied on that group since policies attached to the type-level resource are never consulted. Grants should union, not be shadowed by the existence of an unrelated resource.

adjudication.rationale: In GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission(String groupId, String... scopes), if a per-group Resource exists (resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId) != null), the method evaluates permissions only against that resource. The type-level "all-groups" ResourceType resource (AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(..., GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE)) is only consulted when the per-group resource is missing. Therefore, a caller granted VIEW/MANAGE via the type-level groups resource can be denied for a specific group once that group has its own resource, because the type-level policies are never unioned with the per-group evaluation. This matches the finding and is verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/security] services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:~96 (getGroupIdsWithViewPermission) — the method only scans per-group resources and never consults the type-level resource; an admin granted VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS on 'all groups' (type-level permission, no per-group resources) gets an empty set, which results in an unrestricted user search exposing all users (including those in no group) instead of only group members.

[Medium/data] services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:~180 + AdminPermissions.java:~94 — no cleanup path exists for V2 group authorization data: GroupPermissionsV2 throws UnsupportedOperationException for all permission-management/lifecycle methods, while AdminPermissions.registerListener (registered exactly when V2 is active) still performs cleanup by calling groups().setPermissionsEnabled(group, false) on group removal; deleted groups therefore leave orphaned 'Groups'-type resources and policies behind (which getGroupIdsWithViewPermission keeps scanning), and if the listener resolves to the V2 implementation, every group deletion will throw.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `GroupPermissionsV2` where all permission-management/lifecycle methods (including `setPermissionsEnabled(GroupModel, boolean)`) throw `UnsupportedOperationException` (new file, bottom half). At the same time, `MgmtPermissionsV2.groups()` is overridden to return `GroupPermissionsV2` (MgmtPermissionsV2.java), meaning any code calling `management(...).groups()` in V2 will hit this implementation. `AdminPermissions.registerListener` registers a listener (when `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` is enabled) that, on `GroupModel.GroupRemovedEvent`, calls `management(...).groups().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getGroup(), false)` (AdminPermissions.java). If V2 is active in that runtime, this call will throw, breaking group deletion handling and preventing cleanup of associated authz data. The finding’s concern about orphaned group authz resources/policies is consistent with this missing cleanup path, though the exact resource scanning impact is secondary to the verified exception path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/performance] services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/GroupResource.java:177 and GroupsResource.java:112 — the cached canViewGlobal short-circuit was removed, so filter(...::canView) now runs a full authorization evaluation (resource lookup + policy evaluation) per group element; for admins whose access comes from a type-level grant, getSubGroupsStream(search, exact, -1, -1) loads all subgroups and each one triggers a separate policy evaluation before pagination. canView() should be computed once and used to short-circuit the filter.

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the cached global short-circuit in both `GroupResource.getSubGroups` (replacing `canViewGlobal || auth.groups().canView(g)` with `.filter(auth.groups()::canView)`) and `GroupsResource.getGroups` (replacing `canViewGlobal || groupsEvaluator.canView(g)` with `.filter(groupsEvaluator::canView)`). With the new `GroupPermissionsV2`, `canView(GroupModel)` may perform per-group permission evaluation (`hasPermission(group.getId(), ...)`), so callers whose access is granted via a type-level permission (`canView()` true) lose the “compute once” optimization and may trigger a per-element authz check before pagination (notably `getSubGroupsStream(..., -1, -1)` then filter then paginate). This is a specific, diff-grounded performance regression concern, not a functional correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/security] rest/admin-ui-ext/src/main/java/org/keycloak/admin/ui/rest/BruteForceUsersResource.java:147 — the rewritten searchForUser has the same empty-set overload (empty set → no UserModel.GROUPS attribute → unrestricted search) and, unlike the old UsersResource code, never had a per-user canView filter; the hole is pre-existing, but since these lines are being rewritten to the shared new pattern it should be fixed here too, otherwise admins without view permission get the full user list from the brute-force search.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does not show a new or changed authorization hole in BruteForceUsersResource: before and after, it only sets UserModel.GROUPS when the permitted-groups set is non-empty, and it never had a per-user canView filter. The change is primarily from getGroupsWithViewPermission() to getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() and an early return style; the “empty set → unrestricted search” behavior (if true) is pre-existing and not verifiably introduced or worsened by this diff. Also, whether omitting UserModel.GROUPS actually makes the underlying user search unrestricted is not shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/test_gap] tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/authz/fgap/GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest.java — there is no negative test asserting that an admin holding only the VIEW scope on the Groups resource (no MANAGE) is denied group creation/update/manage; such a test would have caught the canManage() scope bug.

adjudication.rationale: The newly added `GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest` covers positive VIEW behavior (`testViewGroups`) and positive MANAGE behavior (`testManageAllGroups`, `testManageGroup`), but it never asserts the negative case where a principal granted only `VIEW` on the Groups resource type is forbidden from group creation/update/role-mapping. That is a specific, diff-grounded test gap in this PR’s new authorization surface (especially given the new V2 group permission logic).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/doc_defect] services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionEvaluator.java:~147 — the javadoc for getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() says '@return Stream of IDs of groups with view permission', but the method returns Set<String>, not a Stream.

adjudication.rationale: In GroupPermissionEvaluator, the method signature is `Set<String> getGroupIdsWithViewPermission();` but the Javadoc directly above it states `@return Stream of IDs of groups with view permission.` This is a verifiable documentation/type mismatch introduced in the diff; it’s not a runtime defect but a concrete review issue.
